# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 95 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 95 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_095_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 12

**1** "Now I wish to explain to you the stones that were taken from the deep and placed into the building in conjunction with those stones that had already been built," he said. **2** "The first group — the ten stones — represent the first generation; the second group — the twenty-five — represent the second generation of righteous men; **3** the third — the thirty-five — are the prophets of God and his ministers; the fourth — the forty — are apostles and teachers of the proclamation of the Son of God." **4** "But why did the virgins also carry the stones through the gate and give them to build the tower?" I asked. **5** "Because these first ones bore these spirits, and they did not separate from one another — neither the spirits from the men nor the men from the spirits — but the spirits remained with them until they fell asleep. **6** And had the spirits not been with them, they could not have been of use for the building of the tower." **7** "Now explain to me what the tower is," I said. **8** "The tower," he answered, "is, as I told you before, the church." **9** "But those who were rejected — who are they?" **10** "These are those who sinned and wish to repent; for this reason they were not cast far from the tower, because they will be useful for the building if they repent. **11** Those therefore who are going to repent — if they repent now, while the tower is still being built, they will be strong in the faith. **12** But if the tower is completed, they will no longer have a place in it, but will be castoffs. However this privilege — of remaining near the tower — belongs to them on account of affliction; they must be afflicted, for they are not afflicted to no purpose."

---

*LOGOS: the four-generation stone layers (10+25+35+40) embed salvation history into the tower's structure: first righteous → second righteous → prophets → apostles.*
